nodes.name: Copper foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: The preparation of copper foam was initiated by precisely cutting it into squares of 1.5 cm × 1.5 cm. To ensure purity and reactivity, the copper foam underwent a meticulous cleaning process involving anhydrous ethanol, 1 M HCl, and deionized water, sequentially targeting organic pollutants, metal oxides, and residual chemicals.

nodes.name: Ru electrodeposition on copper foam
nodes.procedure: This pristine copper foam was then employed as the working electrode in our electrochemical setup. A Pt plate of 1 cm × 1 cm dimensions served as the counter electrode, while an Ag/AgCl electrode was chosen as the reference. The electrolytic solution comprised 1 M NaOH and 0.25 mM RuCl3. The pivotal step of Ru electrodeposition onto the copper foam was achieved through cyclic voltammetry, spanning a potential range from -0.10 V to -0.40 V versus RHE, and scan rate was 5 mV s^-1, culminating in the formation of the RuSACs-CF electrode.

nodes.description: NO3RR performance across nitrate concentrations (50-1000 mg/L) at optimal potentials
nodes.source_text: RuSACs-CF demonstrates superior catalytic performance across a broad concentration range from 50 to 1000 mg L^{-1}, achieving a peak Faradaic efficiency of 92.6% and NH3 production rate of 2362 μg h^{-1} cm^{-2}. Under various nitrate concentrations, the FENH3 remains no less than 82.2%.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows uniformly distributed particles on surfaces of RuSACs-CF and CF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) results demonstrated the formation of uniformly distributed particles on both the surfaces of RuSACs-CF and CF during the deposition process (Fig. S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM exhibits lattice spacing of 2.05 Å corresponding to the (111) crystal plane of Cu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, high-resolution TEM image exhibited a lattice spacing of 2.05 Å (Fig. 1b), which corresponds to the (111) crystal plane of Cu.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows no discernible Ru lattice and bright spots indicating isolated Ru single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Upon observation of the Ru-CF composite using High-Angle Annular Dark Field Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (HAADF-STEM), no discernible Ru lattice was detected, and bright spots suggesting isolated Ru atoms were visible (Fig. 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows uniform dispersion of Ru, Cu, and O elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopic (EDX) elemental mapping images indicate the uniform dispersion of Ru, Cu, and O in Ru-CF (Fig. 1d and S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of RuSACs-CF and CF match pure Cu with no distinct Ru crystal phase peaks, indicating atomic-level dispersion of Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of both RuSACs-CF and CF are showcased in Fig. S3a. Notably, the XRD profile of Ru-CF and CF aligned closely with that of pure Cu, lacking any distinct diffraction peaks indicative of a Ru crystal phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ru atomic ratio of 6.82% on surface; Cu 2p peaks at 932.5 eV and 952.1 eV indicate Cu0 state; Ru 3p peaks at 462.0/484.1 eV (Ru4+) and 486.3/464.1 eV indicate mixed valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS full-spectrum analysis revealed that the atomic ratio of Ru atoms on the surface of RuSACs-CF is 6.82%. Analyzing the Cu 2p XPS spectrum (Fig. S3b), a pair of peaks at binding energies of 932.5 eV and 952.1 eV... In the Ru 3p XPS spectrum, peaks at binding energies of 462.0 eV and 484.1 eV corresponded to Ru4+.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS at Ru K-edge shows prominent peak at 1.5 Å indicating Ru-O coordination; absence of Ru-Ru coordination at 2.3 Å confirms atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS spectrum of RuSACs-CF revealed a prominent peak at 1.5 Å, signifying Ru-O coordination (Fig. 1e and S5). Unlike the EXAFS spectrum of Ru foil, the absence of Ru-Ru coordination around 2.3 Å in RuSACs-CF confirmed the atomic dispersion of Ru atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES indicates Ru valence state approximates +4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, analysis using Ru K-edge XANES indicated that valence state of Ru approximates more closely to +4 (Fig. 1f and S6), aligning well with the findings obtained from XPS analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: Wavelet transform plot shows maximum intensity from Ru-O scattering at 3.9 Å, confirming atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This atomic dispersion of Ru was further corroborated by the wavelet transform (WT) plot, where the maximum intensity stemming from Ru-O scattering is observed at 3.9 Å (Fig. 1g and S6).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at varying scan rates used to calculate ECSA of 6.01 mF cm^-2 for RuSACs-CF (higher than CF and Cu at 1.30 mF cm^-2), indicating Ru single atoms augment ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: electrochemical specific surface areas (ECSAs) of the catalysts were calculated using cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements at varying scan rates [54]. ... As shown in Fig. 3e, the ECSA of RuSACs-CF (6.01 mF cm^-2) surpassed that of CF and Cu (1.30 mF cm^-2)

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots show smaller semicircle radius (lower charge transfer resistance) for RuSACs-CF compared to Cu and CF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To gain deeper insights into the electrochemical behavior of RuSACs-CF, Nyquist plots were obtained using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (Fig. 3f). The analysis of these plots revealed that the radius of the semicircle... was smaller for RuSACs-CF than Cu and CF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Auger electron spectroscopy (AES) with Cu LMM spectrum confirms Cu 2p peaks at 932.5 eV and 952.1 eV correspond to Cu0 state in RuSACs-CF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A closer analysis, coupled with the Cu LMM spectrum, confirmed their association with the Cu0 state (Fig. S4).
